title: luastream://
description:
`luastream://`: Lua code whose `print()` / `io.write()` output (or `dbdash.emit()`) is
the data, item by item. Runs Lua, so it asks for trust first. See
`:help dbdash-luastream`.

query.sql:
-- One reading per second for a minute, as JSON lines.
for i = 1, 60 do
  print(vim.json.encode({ at = os.date("%H:%M:%S"), load = 40 + math.random(0, 30) }))
  dbdash.sleep(1000)
end
query.transform:
-- Each item is one line; keep the last 30 readings in store to draw them.
store.points = store.points or {}
table.insert(store.points, vim.json.decode(rs))
while #store.points > 30 do table.remove(store.points, 1) end
return store.points

show.title: print(): one reading per second
show.description:
One JSON row printed per second; the panel shows new data at most once per
`interval`.

query.sql:
-- Count the lines of a file in cwd, written as items separated by ";".
local n = 0
for _ in io.lines("events.schema.yaml") do n = n + 1 end
io.write("lines=" .. n .. ";")
io.write("dir=" .. dbdash.cwd .. ";")
-- dbdash.emit: one item as it is, no cutting (the last item: the code ends).
dbdash.emit({ { key = "done", value = os.date("%H:%M:%S") } })

show.title: io.write() with a delimiter, dbdash.emit(), cwd
show.description:
`io.write()` with `delimiter: ";"`, `dbdash.emit()` for a value as it is, and `cwd`
for `dbdash.cwd()`.

query.sql:
-- A temperature every 2 seconds, in Celsius.
for i = 1, 600 do
  print(vim.json.encode({ celsius = 15 + math.random(0, 100) / 10 }))
  dbdash.sleep(2000)
end
query.transform:
local c = vim.json.decode(rs).celsius
local value = args.unit == "F" and c * 9 / 5 + 32 or c
if meta.run.kind == "callback" then
  return { { value = value } }                  -- for the caller below
end
-- the same item again, in the other unit
local other = args.unit == "F" and "C" or "F"
local again = dbdash.run({ unit = other }).rows[1][1]
return { columns = { "reading", "other unit" },
         rows = { { ("%.1f °%s"):format(value, args.unit),
                    ("%.1f °%s"):format(again, other) } } }

show.title: dbdash.run(): the same item in the other unit
show.description:
`dbdash.run({ unit = ... })` in `query.transform` takes the current item again with
another argument. Change the unit with `:DbDashUpdateVariable unit F`.
